newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS confirms Inco ratings, stable outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBRS confirms Inco ratings, stable outlook.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it confirmed the ratings on Inco Ltd's senior unsecured debentures and term notes, convertible debentures and preferred shares at B++(High), B++ and P-3, respectively, with a stable outlook.

CBRS said the retention of the medium-quality credit ratings reflect Inco's leading position in the world nickel industry and favorable operating leverage, the enhancement in long life reserves (after Voisey's Bay acquisition), and the maintenance of financial flexibility during the 1990s.

"However, the company's continuing strength in cashflow generation and its recent and expected divestitures should moderate the requirement for external financing during the three-year period while maintaining the credit standing of its debt and preferred securities," CBRS said.

It said Inco is expected to generate an acceptable level of earnings, cashflow and coverage levels in 1997. The resumption of nickel demand should help inventory drawdown and maintain an average pricing in the US$3.50 to US$3.75 per pound range.

The near-term challenge for Inco is to continue development of high-grade material from its existing nickel mines, lower its unit production costs, and reach an amicable settlement with its workforce in Ontario.
Inco's current contract is slated to end May 31, 1997.

"Partly offsetting factors, which affect the financial performance include the cyclicality of nickel demand in its core operations, the price fluctuations and an average cost structure of Inco, which is not expected to change dramatically until the commencement of (the) Voisey's Bay project in 2000," CBRS said.

It said the construction phase of Voisey's Bay project was slated to cost US$1.4 billion which, combined with Inco's current and anticipated investment plans in 1997-1999, would result in higher debt leverage from its year-end 1996 position of 22 percent (equity 78 percent).
